name: Motion camera trap
summary: An M5Stack Timer Camera that sleeps until a PIR sensor sees movement, then takes a photo; a month on one 18650 cell in a printed weatherproof box.

spec.name: Motion Camera Trap
spec.function: Photographs whatever moves in the garden: the ESP32 camera sleeps until the HC-SR505 PIR sensor sees movement, wakes, takes a picture, saves or sends it over Wi-Fi and goes back to sleep, from one 18650 cell in a holder that charges it over USB-C and boosts it to 5 V.
spec.quote: I want the ESP32-CAM PIR camera from Random Nerd Tutorials as a proper garden camera trap: a printed box with a rain lip that stands on a shelf or screws to a fence, running on an 18650 so I don't need a cable. It should last at least a month on one charge with about 20 visits a day, cost under 40 euros, weigh under 300 grams and not blow over.

parts.name: Housing
parts.description: Upright box 70 x 45 x 110 mm centred on X=Y=0 on the stand (Z 4 to 114), open at the back (+Y), 2.4 mm walls, a 12 mm lens hole at Z 98 and a 10.6 mm PIR hole at Z 72 in the front wall, a rain lip over the lens and four screw bosses for the back lid.

parts.name: Back lid
parts.description: Plate 70 x 2.4 x 110 mm closing the back of the housing (Y 22.5 to 24.9), with four M2.5 holes, a USB-C charging hole and a keyhole to hang it on a fence screw.

parts.name: Stand
parts.description: Foot plate 110 x 90 x 4 mm centred on X=Y=0 (Z 0 to 4) under the housing, with four screw holes.

parts.name: ESP32 camera board
parts.description: Lies across the top of the housing, lens in the front hole

parts.name: PIR motion sensor
parts.description: Wakes the camera; its lens sits in the front hole

parts.name: 18650 holder with USB-C charger and 5 V boost
parts.description: Stands upright in the lower half of the housing

requirements.text: Runs at least 30 days on one charge with 20 visits a day
requirements.quote: It should last at least a month on one charge with about 20 visits a day

camera.reason: ESP32 camera with a real-time clock and deep sleep in microwatts, wakes on a GPIO from the PIR; the bare ESP32-CAM is out of stock at Berrybase today.

pir.reason: Mini PIR that fits a 10.6 mm hole and draws under 60 uA while it waits; the HC-SR501 is sold out.

cell.reason: One 3000 mAh 18650 holds a month of 20 photos a day.

holder.reason: Charges the cell over USB-C through the back lid and boosts it to the camera's 5 V.
